# All Out (2021) — AEW Pay-Per-View Event

**All Out** is an annual pay-per-view event produced by **All Elite Wrestling (AEW)**. The 2021 edition took place on **September 5, 2021**, at the **Now Arena** (formerly Sears Centre) in **Hoffman Estates, Illinois** (near Chicago).

---

## Key Details

- **Date:** September 5, 2021 (Labor Day Weekend)
- **Venue:** Now Arena, Hoffman Estates, Illinois
- **Attendance:** Approximately 11,000+
- **Broadcast:** Pay-per-view and on Bleacher Report Live

---

## Card and Results

### CM Punk vs. Darby Allin
- One of the most anticipated matches of the night
- CM Punk's **second match back** in AEW (his in-ring return had occurred on the prior Rampage)
- **Punk won**
- The feud was significant given Punk's Chicago connection and massive crowd reaction

### Kenny Omega vs. Christian Cage (AEW World Championship)
- Kenny Omega defended the AEW World Championship
- **Omega retained** with interference from Don Callis and the Elite
- Christian had been a strong challenger

### Dr. Britt Baker D.M.D. vs. Kris Statlander (AEW Women's World Championship)
- Baker defended her title
- **Baker retained**

### The Young Bucks (Matt & Nick Jackson) vs. Lucha Brothers (Pentagon Jr. & Rey Fenix) — Ladder Match (AEW World Tag Team Championship)
- Arguably the match of the night for many fans
- Extremely high-risk, spot-heavy ladder match
- **The Lucha Brothers won** the AEW World Tag Team Championships
- Considered one of the best tag team ladder matches in recent memory

### Miro vs. Eddie Kingston (TNT Championship)
- Miro defended the TNT Championship
- **Miro retained**

### Cage of Agony (Brian Cage, Ricky Starks, Hook, Kayla Rosenbohm) vs. Team Sting (Sting, Darby Allin, and others) — I believe this may need clarification; let me note Sting/Darby had various involvements around this time

### MJF vs. Chris Jericho — Stadium Stampede or other stipulation
*(I want to be careful here — their specific match details at this event I may be conflating with other events)*

### Bryan Danielson Debut
- One of the **biggest surprises** of the night
- **Bryan Danielson** (formerly Daniel Bryan in WWE) debuted in AEW at the end of the show
- He appeared after the main event, confronting wrestlers in the ring
- This was a massive moment given his WWE history and star power

### Adam Cole Debut
- **Adam Cole** also debuted at the event, surprising fans
- He appeared alongside the Elite, with connections to the Young Bucks and Kenny Omega from their PWG/ROH days
- "**Adam Cole Bay Bay**" chants erupted
- This was another landmark signing for AEW

---

## Significance

- The **dual debuts of Bryan Danielson and Adam Cole** made this one of the most talked-about AEW events ever
- The show was considered a landmark moment in the **Wednesday Night Wars** era and AEW's growth
- The Lucha Brothers ladder match was widely praised
- CM Punk's continued integration into AEW was a major ongoing story
- The event helped solidify AEW as a major player in professional wrestling

---

## Overall Reception

The event received **very strong reviews** from fans and critics. The surprise debuts, combined with strong in-ring work (particularly the ladder match), made it one of AEW's highest-praised pay-per-view events up to that point.

---

I'd recommend cross-referencing with a wrestling database like Cagematch or Wikipedia for a complete and fully accurate card.*
